text.content:
A spirit is a trait, not a creature type (Pillars of Faith, Chapter 8). A spirit that fights uses a creature stat block — give it the Spirit trait.

A spirit that exists principally as an NPC, a source of information or an influence is a Spirit Presence. Drag Spirit Presence (Template) from Pillars of Faith: Haunts & Spirits, rename it, set its level, and fill in the ten lines in its GM notes. Placed as a token, it can be targeted by Read Spirit Signs, Trace Possession and Interpret Haunt, which roll against its Level DC (level + 14).

Social actions, offerings, attitudes, possession, banishment and destruction use the ordinary rules of whatever ability is involved.

A haunt is a peril: an NPC with its Peril section on, on the GM tab. The nine sample haunts in Pillars of Faith: Haunts & Spirits are filled in from the book; to build your own, type its stat block's lines into the same fields.

  • Detection line — each skill with its DC, as printed ("Perception DC 17; Occultism or Religion DC 17, Rank 1"). Roll Detection makes a secret check for each PC on the scene with the skill that serves them best; a PC whose Spirit Sense reaches the haunt is told of its presence and direction without a roll.
  • Disable line — any skill, each with its DC, a specialist Lore by name ("Spirit Lore"). Players target the haunt and use Disable a Peril from that skill; a Critical counts two successes, a Heroic three; a Fumble or Blunder triggers it. When the last success lands the haunt is suppressed for its span ("Suppressed for"), or until its next Reset when none is printed.
  • Counteract — Dispel, Still the Haunt and Quarantine Working counteract it at its level and Level DC, and suppress it for the effect's own span.
  • Trigger — rolls the Effect: everyone within a printed radius of the haunt's token, or the creatures you have targeted (the triggering creature, those in the room), save against the printed DC or its Level DC; the conditions and damage of their rung are applied. A complex haunt joins the combat and rolls Initiative; on its turn, Use each of its routine actions (abilities on its sheet) with the right creatures targeted.
  • Suppression — a suppressed haunt cannot trigger or act. A span in hours or minutes re-arms itself as game time passes; "until sunrise", "at midnight" and "until its next Reset" wait for your Reset.
  • Resolve — when the party meets its Resolution, press Resolve: it is ended for good and never resets.
  • No body — a haunt cannot be struck; its Anchor, if it has statistics, is a separate object or creature.

XP: as a peril of its level, once, on the Party sheet.

What the haunts print that is not a condition, a save or damage is on their cards for you to rule on: being unable to approach a bed or cross a threshold, false convictions, compelled confessions, being pushed by the Surging Crowd, being unable to speak, singing with the choir, the Watchman's countersign and his grudge, a forgotten skill or memory, and what destroying an Anchor does.

The Hungry Reliquary's Effect heals the creature you target and drains a random living creature within 60 feet; Redistribute Suffering heals the most injured creature within 60 feet and drains another, who makes a Basic Will save.
